info.title: Leadstaker API
info.description: Public REST API for Leadstaker projects.

tags.name: Calls
tags.description: Phone calls made through the telephony app, with their recording, transcript and AI summary.

tags.name: Chats
tags.description: Conversations with a contact over a connected channel.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: People inside a project, holding the custom field values collected about them.

tags.name: Deals
tags.description: Opportunities moving through a pipeline, each tied to a contact.

tags.name: Field groups
tags.description: Sections that organize custom fields in the interface.

tags.name: Fields
tags.description: Custom field definitions, both the built-in ones and the ones a project creates.

tags.name: Leads
tags.description: Chatbot conversations captured in a project, with the answers given and where the visitor came from.

tags.name: Loss reasons
tags.description: The catalog of reasons a deal can be marked as lost.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: Individual messages inside a chat, inbound and outbound.

tags.name: Notes
tags.description: Free text attached to a contact or a deal, written by a user, an agent, or the system.

tags.name: Pipelines
tags.description: Ordered sets of stages a deal travels through.

tags.name: Stages
tags.description: Steps inside a pipeline, including the built-in open and closed ones.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Follow-up activities with a due date, attached to a deal and assigned to a user.

get.description: Answers with a bare array of calls, newest first, without an envelope or pagination fields. A call is stored once it ends, with its recording copied a few seconds later. Answered calls up to one hour are transcribed on their own; each transcription is followed by an AI summary in `analysis`. That analysis also writes what the call said into the fields of the deal and the contact, filled ones included, so a call can raise the same update events and webhooks as any other edit. Only the calls attached to this deal come back.

get.description: Answers with a bare array of calls, newest first, without an envelope or pagination fields. A call is stored once it ends, with its recording copied a few seconds later. Answered calls up to one hour are transcribed on their own; each transcription is followed by an AI summary in `analysis`. That analysis also writes what the call said into the fields of the deal and the contact, filled ones included, so a call can raise the same update events and webhooks as any other edit. Includes the calls attached to the contact and to the deals of the contact the caller can see.

patch.description: Sets the chat status to CLOSED. Answers 204 with no body.

patch.summary: Turn the AI agent on or off for a chat, or switch it
patch.description: Sets the AI agent of the chat to ACTIVE or DISABLED. With `agentId`, switches the chat to that agent of the project (404 when there is none, or it is archived; 422 TEST_CHAT on a test chat): it takes the `status` given, else the one the chat had, else ACTIVE, and what the previous agent had queued for the chat (follow-ups, a reply being sent) is dropped. The agent the chat already has only changes the status. Answers 204 with no body.

status.description: ACTIVE or DISABLED. Required without `agentId`; with it, the chat keeps its status when absent (ACTIVE for a chat that had no agent).

agentId.description: Switches the chat to this agent of the project. The chat's current agent only changes the status.

parameters.description: Free-text search across the contact fields.

parameters.name: fieldFilters
parameters.description: Conditions on field values, as a JSON array of `{ fieldId, fieldType?, operator, value? }`, all of which must hold. Operators: equals, not_equals, contains, not_contains, gt, gte, lt, lte, between (`from|to`), is_true, is_false, is_empty, is_not_empty. A CONTACT:PHONE equals matches the number with or without the Brazilian ninth digit. Ignored by `search`.

get.description: Answers with the paginated envelope: the matching contacts in `data`, plus `hasMore`, `limit`, `offset` and `total`.

post.description: Creates the contact in the project of the API key. Upsert: answers 200 with the existing contact when one already matches, instead of 201 with a duplicate.

value.description: The value in the shape of the field's type. TEXT, PHONE, EMAIL, CPF, CNPJ, CPF_CNPJ, CEP, LINK and OPTIONS: a string (OPTIONS: one of its options). NUMBER: a number. CURRENCY: an amount in reais, as a number or a decimal string (`1500.5`, `"1.500,50"`), rounded to the cent. It is stored and read back in cents (`150050`). BOOLEAN: `true` or `false`. MULTISELECT: an array of its options. DATE and DATETIME: `YYYY-MM-DD`, an ISO 8601 datetime (UTC when it has no offset) or epoch milliseconds, stored as a date. TIME: `HH:mm`. `null` clears the field. A value that does not fit its field, or a `fieldId` this kind of record does not have, answers 422 naming the field.

messageIds.description: Ids the queued messages will be stored under, in order. Empty for AI, which writes its own.

delivery.description: REPORTED when the calling automation step will be told how the send went.

post.description: Starts or reuses a chat for the number and answers with its id and the ids the queued messages will be stored under; delivery is queued. `MESSAGES` sends a sequence in order, one message after the other: each item a text, or a typed message (text or media) as `MESSAGE` takes it, every type checked against the chat before anything is queued. A request repeated by the same caller with the same `Idempotency-Key` header and body answers from the first run instead of sending again; the key with a different body answers 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.

deliveryTimeoutMs.description: Automations only: how long the calling step waits to hear how the send went. A message still queued by then is not sent, and the step is told it failed with DELIVERY_TIMEOUT.

messages.description: Sent in order, one after the other. Each is a text, or a typed message (text or media: IMAGE, VIDEO, AUDIO, DOCUMENT, ...) as `MESSAGE` takes it; `messageIds` answers one id per item, in the same order.

createdByAutomation.description: The workflow run that created the task, when an automation did; `createdBy` names users only.

post.description: Creates the task in the project of the API key and answers 201 with the created record. `dueAt` is an ISO 8601 instant and needs an explicit offset (`Z` or `±hh:mm`), so a local time with no offset is rejected. `createdBy` is filled only when a user creates the task, so it stays absent for an API key. `responsibleId` may name another user only when the caller is a project owner or admin: any other user must send their own id, otherwise answers 403 `UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS`. An API key is not restricted. Answers 404 `DEAL` when `dealId` is not in the project.

dealId.description: The deal the task belongs to.

dueAt.description: ISO 8601 instant with an explicit offset, e.g. 2026-09-20T17:00:00Z or 2026-09-20T14:00:00-03:00.

parameters.name: status[in]
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of `pending | overdue | completed`, answered as their union. Omit it to filter nothing by status.

parameters.name: overdueBefore[lt]
parameters.description: The instant a task counts as overdue, at most the current time. Defaults to now and only weighs when `overdue` is listed.

createdByAutomation.description: The workflow run that created the task, when an automation did; `createdBy` names users only.

items.description: Custom field value for this entity

get.description: Answers with the paginated envelope: the matching tasks in `data`, plus `hasMore`, `limit`, `offset` and `total`. `status[in]` selects whole statuses instead of raw fields: `pending` is a task with no `completedAt`, `overdue` is a pending one already past `overdueBefore`, and `completed` is one with `completedAt`. Listing several answers their union, so `overdue,completed` needs no `[logic]`, and every other filter still applies on top. `deal` comes back only when `[with]=deal` is sent.

createdByAutomation.description: The workflow run that created the task, when an automation did; `createdBy` names users only.

get.description: Answers 404 when the id does not exist or belongs to another project.

patch.description: Partial update: only the keys present in the body change. Answers 204 with no body. The result is set on completion, so `result` is ignored here. `dueAt` can be changed, in the same ISO 8601 instant format as the creation, by the current responsible or a project owner or admin: any other user answers 403 `UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS`, while the stored instant sent again is not a change. A completed task cannot be changed: answers 422 `TASK_COMPLETED`. Handing the task to another user (a `responsibleId` different from the stored one) needs a project owner or admin: any other user answers 403 `UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS`, while the current value sent again is not a change. An API key is not restricted.

dueAt.description: ISO 8601 instant with an explicit offset, e.g. 2026-09-20T17:00:00Z or 2026-09-20T14:00:00-03:00.

delete.description: The task is deleted. Answers 204 with no body.

createdByAutomation.description: The workflow run that created the task, when an automation did; `createdBy` names users only.

post.description: Records `completedAt` and the `result`, which is required and holds at most 2000 characters. `completedBy` is filled only when a user completes the task, so it stays absent for an API key. Completing an already completed task changes nothing and answers the task as stored.

result.description: What was done or decided, at most 2000 characters.

durationInSeconds.description: Talk time, from the answer to the hang up.

status.description: `PENDING` while the recording is copied from the provider; only a `STORED` one can be played or transcribed.
`AVAILABLE`: can be requested. `TOO_LONG`: the recording is over the transcription limit. `PENDING`, `DONE` or `FAILED` once requested.

text.description: The whole transcript in one block, when the call was not split by speaker. Absent when `turns` is present.

speaker.description: `SELLER` is the extension side, `CUSTOMER` the phone side.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the recording.

turns.description: Who said what, in order. Present when each side of the call was transcribed from its own channel of the recording.

transcription.description: Null while there is no stored recording.

summary.description: Absent when the call had nothing worth summing up, such as a voicemail.

analysis.description: The AI summary, written after each transcription; null before the first one.

post.description: Queues the transcription of a call that has none yet, or whose last one failed, and answers with the call in `PENDING`. Calls over one hour are not transcribed on their own, so this is how to get theirs. A transcription already pending or done answers the call as it is, without queuing another. Answers 404 `RECORDING` while the recording is not `STORED`, and 422 `TELEPHONY_CALL_TOO_LONG` when it is over the size the transcription accepts (about 1h40).
